paragraphs: Dartford is in Kent, so children in care from the town are looked after by Kent County Council's fostering service, Kent Fostering, and by the independent agencies shown above. The council says the number of children in its care is growing and that many need a home in their own community, whether for a night, a few months or several years. It has also pointed to a regional shortage of 820 foster carers across the South East.

You do not need formal qualifications to foster for Kent, although experience of children or of caring for others helps. You must live in the UK full time or have leave to remain, have a spare room and be able to give your time, often full time. The council describes its support as round-the-clock help, local training, career progression, holiday entitlement and a team that stays with you from your first enquiry.

Kent publishes its 2026-27 rates, set by a Cabinet Member decision in April 2026. The weekly maintenance allowance for each child runs from £210 for a child under two to £320.92 for a young person over 16. Carers looking after children who are not related to them also receive a weekly reward payment of £156.70 for a child aged up to eight and £297.64 for a child aged nine to 18, with skills payments for carers at Levels 2 and 3 and a disability enhancement where it applies. Our Kent allowance page has every figure.

Our Kent page covers the county as a whole, and the Bexley page covers the London borough next door. Speak to Kent Fostering and to two or three of the services above about the children they most need homes for, their training and the support they give.
